case_text:
Vignette:
A 35-year-old man who is an avid hiker in Connecticut presents with a 5-day history of an expanding red rash on his right thigh that he noticed after a weekend camping trip two weeks ago. He recalls removing an engorged tick from his thigh. He now reports fatigue, mild headache, arthralgias in his knees and wrists, and low-grade fever. He denies neck stiffness, facial weakness, chest pain, or palpitations. On examination, temperature is 99.6°F. There is a 12 cm annular erythematous plaque on the right anterior thigh with central clearing, consistent with erythema migrans. There are no secondary skin lesions. Joints are nontender without effusion. Neurological examination is nonfocal. Heart rate is regular at 74 with no murmurs. There is no cervical rigidity.
